title: Run a gas furnace from a generator or inverter
summary: A gas furnace needs a few hundred watts of clean 120 V power, plus a start-up surge, to heat a house in a power cut. Feed it through a CSA-certified transfer switch fitted by a licensed electrician, or run it on its own cord with nothing joined to house wiring, never by backfeeding a cord into a wall or dryer outlet, and keep the generator outside and well away from windows. A furnace that lights and then shuts off on generator power usually can't sense its flame because of a floating neutral or bad ground.

materials.item: Portable generator, preferably an inverter generator, rated well above the furnace's running watts
Or a pure sine wave inverter with a battery bank sized for the furnace

CSA-certified transfer switch (a manual transfer switch, or a plug-in transfer device at the meter base) fitted by a licensed electrician; or, for the furnace alone, no house connection at all, just a heavy flex cord and plug on the furnace as in the ESA diagram
Power inlet box and generator cord with matching locking plugs
Heavy, grounded three-prong extension cord rated for the load, laid flat and uncoiled
Neutral-ground bonding plug: last resort for a furnace fed by cord from a floating-neutral generator that feeds nothing else; never with a transfer switch or any connection to house wiring

steps.text: Read the furnace's rating plate and blower label: volts, blower motor amps, and the maximum fuse or breaker size. For example, Rheem lists its R801P blower motors at 5.7 to 9.3 A at 115 V (Rheem R801P spec), and Lennox lists 6.8 to 10.9 A for the ML180UHE blower and a 15 A maximum breaker (Lennox 1120).

Size the source. DTE's planning guide puts a furnace fan at 400 W (1/4 hp) to 600 W (1/2 hp) running, and says to allow 3 times that to start it (DTE appliance guide). Add the inducer fan, igniter and board, and anything else on the same circuit.
steps.warn: An inverter or small generator that can't start the blower trips or stalls. Size for the start, not just the running watts.

steps.text: Use clean power. Lennox asks for 102 to 132 V, 57 to 63 Hz and a waveform with less than 5% total harmonic distortion on generator power (Lennox EL297UHV). Use a pure sine wave inverter, not a modified sine one (Samlex sine).

Get the connection made properly. In Canada that means a CSA-certified transfer switch (a manual transfer switch, or a plug-in transfer device at the meter base) fitted by a licensed electrician. Or leave the house wiring out of it: ESA's diagram for a gas or oil furnace puts the furnace on its own cord and plug so the generator plugs in where the furnace's wall plug was, and ESA says a cord-connected gas appliance also needs a separate bonding conductor on the gas pipe (ESA Flash 25-15-FL; ESA toolbox talk). In Ontario, ESA requires a transfer device and a notification for any permanent generator connection (ESA generators); BC Hydro requires a CSA-approved transfer switch installed under permit (BC Hydro backup).
steps.warn: Never feed house wiring through a wall outlet, a dryer outlet or a cord with a plug on both ends. Backfeed can electrocute line workers and neighbours on your transformer (CPSC 5123), and the generator can burn or explode when power returns (Honda EU2200i).

steps.text: Put the generator outside, at least 6 m (20 ft) from the house, with its exhaust pointing away from doors, windows, vents and air intakes (Health Canada CO, Honda EU2200i, ESA toolbox talk). In wet or snowy weather keep it dry under an open canopy-like cover, never in an enclosed space, and keep its vents clear of snow and debris (CPSC 5123, Honda EU2200i). Fit battery CO alarms inside, on every level and outside sleeping areas (Honda EU2200i).
steps.warn: Never run it in a house, garage, shed, basement, crawl space or any enclosed or partly enclosed space, even with doors and windows open: CO builds up fast and lingers for hours (CPSC 5123, Honda EU2200i, Health Canada CO).

steps.text: Before switching over: turn the thermostat down, switch the furnace off at its service switch, start the generator and let it settle, switch off the other big loads, then move the transfer switch to generator (or plug the furnace's own cord into the generator) and bring loads on one at a time (ESA toolbox talk).

Prove the power at the furnace before you run it. Lennox says to check polarity and ground before running the furnace on temporary power (Lennox EL297UHV). With your meter at a plug or receptacle on that circuit, not inside the furnace's junction box: hot to neutral about 120 V, hot to ground about 120 V, neutral to ground close to 0 V. A plug-in outlet tester will show open ground on a floating-neutral generator plugged in directly; Generac calls that normal (Generac neutral).
steps.warn: If you must probe inside the furnace, its supply terminals stay live with the blower door off, and Goodman warns that multiple power sources may be present (Goodman RS6621301). One hand, insulated probes, touch nothing else ([Isolating mains](#guides/safety_mains_isolation)).

steps.text: Turn the furnace on and raise the thermostat. Watch the start: inducer fan, a purge, the igniter glowing, then the burners lighting and the blower coming on. On the Lennox EL297UHV the purge is about 15 seconds and the igniter warms for about 20 (Lennox EL297UHV).

If the burners light and go out after a few seconds, and it keeps retrying, the board isn't sensing flame. Goodman says a missing earth ground, reversed polarity or a high-resistance neutral can cause exactly that lockout (Goodman RS6621301). Recheck polarity and the neutral-to-ground reading. A coating on the flame sensor causes the same lockout; Goodman says it is cleaned with emery cloth or steel wool, with the power off (Goodman IO-359J).
steps.warn: After three failed tries the Goodman control locks out and resets itself after an hour, or when power is cut for 1 to 20 seconds (Goodman IO-359J). Don't keep cycling it.

steps.text: Still locking out, with polarity and ground right, on a floating-neutral generator (Honda lists the EU2200i that way; Generac says most inverter generators are)? For a furnace fed by cord from the generator alone, some people fit a neutral-ground bonding plug in a spare generator outlet. That is this guide's own reasoning from Generac, Goodman and Lennox, not a furnace maker's instruction: Generac mentions bonding plugs only for RV-type use (Generac neutral), and a trade safety site calls them untested, unlisted and easy to leave half-pulled (e-Hazard). Treat it as a last resort, with nothing else on that generator, and measure again: neutral to ground should read near 0 V.
steps.warn: Never with a transfer switch or any link to house wiring, and unplug it before you make one. The house panel already has the bond; a second bond makes a loop that can trip the generator's GFCI (Generac GFCI).

steps.text: Refuel the generator only when it is stopped and has cooled, outdoors, and wipe up any spill before starting it (Honda EU2200i).
To go back: thermostat down, let the blower finish its run, furnace switch off, transfer switch back to the grid, then stop the generator.

notes:
## What a furnace draws

| Part | What it does | Power |
|---|---|---|
| Blower motor | Moves the warm air: the biggest load | Rheem R801P: 1/3 to 3/4 hp PSC motors, 5.7 to 9.3 A at 115 V, listed as 248 to 560 W (Rheem R801P spec). Lennox ML180UHE: brushless (ECM) motors, 6.8 to 10.9 A (Lennox 1120) |
| Inducer fan | Pulls combustion gas through the heat exchanger and out the vent | 120 V from the control board (Goodman RS6621301) |
| Hot-surface igniter | Glows to light the gas, for about 20 seconds each start (Lennox EL297UHV) | 120 V during warm-up (Goodman RS6621301) |
| Control board and 24 V transformer | Runs the sequence and senses the flame | 40 VA transformer, 120 V in, 24 V out (Lennox 1120) |

For planning, DTE lists a central furnace fan at 400 W (1/4 hp), 450 W (1/3 hp) or 600 W (1/2 hp) running, with a starting factor of 3 (DTE appliance guide). Lennox's maximum breaker for these furnaces is 15 A (Lennox 1120), and a 15 A circuit at 120 V tops out at about 1,800 W. Check your furnace's own plate. See [Power budgets](#guides/reference_power_budget) and [Power draw](#guides/reference_power_draw) for sizing batteries and inverters.

## Why a furnace won't run on some generators

Modern furnaces prove the flame by flame rectification: a probe in the flame passes a tiny current, 1 to 6 microamps on the Goodman, that the control reads (Goodman IO-359J). For flame rectification the control's 24 V common is grounded to the cabinet (Goodman RS6621301), and Goodman's check for proper grounding is less than 10 Ω between the neutral wire and the burner nearest the flame sensor, power off (Goodman RS6621301). Goodman says a missing earth ground, reversed polarity or a high-resistance neutral can make the control lock out because it can't sense the flame (Goodman RS6621301). On house wiring that tie is made at the main panel (Generac GFCI), and Goodman's own test, neutral to the burner nearest the flame sensor under 10 ohms with the power off, goes through a ground wire it says must run all the way back to the electrical panel (Goodman RS6621301). Lennox says the same board needs correct polarity and proper ground on temporary power (Lennox EL297UHV).

Some portable generators have a **floating neutral**: the winding is isolated from the frame and the ground pin. Honda's EU2200i and Generac's inverter models are built this way (Honda EU2200i; Generac neutral). Others are **bonded**, with the neutral tied to the frame, such as Generac's open-frame models (Generac neutral). The owner's manual says which (Generac neutral).
- **Through a transfer switch that leaves the house neutral connected**, the house panel's own neutral-ground bond gives the furnace its reference. A bonded generator here, with the bond in the home's main panel, sets up a loop and its GFCI may trip; Generac's fixes are a switched-neutral kit or having a dealer remove the generator's bond (Generac GFCI).
- **Straight from the generator by cord**, with no house panel in the path, a floating-neutral generator gives the furnace no neutral-to-ground tie (Honda EU2200i; Generac neutral). ESA's diagram for running a gas or oil furnace this way calls for three-prong plugs and cords "to ensure proper bonding" and a separate bonding conductor on the gas pipe (ESA Flash 25-15-FL). Some people also add a bonding plug, a plug with its neutral pin joined to its ground pin, in a spare generator outlet. That step is this guide's own reasoning, not a furnace maker's instruction: Generac mentions bonding plugs only for RV-type use (Generac neutral), and e-Hazard warns they are untested, unlisted and easy to leave part-pulled (e-Hazard). If you try one, use it only on a generator that feeds the furnace and nothing else, check that neutral to ground then reads near 0 V, and take it out before the generator is ever joined to house wiring.

## Clean power

Furnace controls and ECM blowers are electronics. Lennox asks for less than 5% THD on generator power (Lennox EL297UHV). A modified sine wave inverter's output carries high-frequency harmonics that heat motors more, and devices whose control circuits sense the phase for voltage or speed control may not work properly on it (Samlex sine). Use a pure sine wave inverter or an inverter generator, and check the generator's spec for its distortion.

## Getting connected the right way

- A transfer device stops generator power flowing back into the utility lines (ESA generators). Generac names a dryer outlet as another improper way to wire a generator into a house (Generac backfeed). Honda says standby connections to a building must be made by a qualified electrician and must isolate the generator from utility power (Honda EU2200i). A cord with a plug on both ends, sold for backfeeding, is what CPSC tells people to stop using and throw away (CPSC cords).
- In Ontario, ESA requires a transfer device for a generator permanently connected to house wiring, and a notification filed with ESA; it strongly recommends a licensed electrical contractor (ESA generators). BC Hydro says a CSA-approved transfer switch needs an electrical permit to install (BC Hydro backup).
- Small plug-in inverters can't be connected to a breaker panel; large ones can, through a transfer switch (BC Hydro backup). Panel interlock kits are a US method: Schneider Electric says Canadian load centres have no interlock kit accessory (Schneider FAQ), and the safe options ESA lists are a whole-home transfer system, a manual transfer switch or a meter-mounted device (ESA toolbox talk).
- Cords: grounded three-prong, rated for the load, uncoiled and laid flat, since coiled cords get very hot (ESA generators).

The 240 V panel, the meter base and anything upstream of the main breaker are not places to learn. If nobody competent is left, don't connect a generator to panels, switches or service equipment without a transfer mechanism (ESA toolbox talk). The smaller job is the one in ESA's diagram: the furnace on its own cord and plug, with the generator plugged in where the furnace's wall plug was, so nothing from the generator can reach house wiring. ESA says the permanent receptacle in that diagram must meet code and be inspected, that the furnace's branch breaker goes off before its wiring is altered, and that every conductor is treated as live in case main power returns (ESA Flash 25-15-FL; see [Isolating mains](#guides/safety_mains_isolation)).

## Where the generator goes

Outside, at least 6 m (20 ft) from the house, exhaust away from doors, windows and vents, with the windows and doors nearest it closed (Health Canada CO). Honda says to run it outside, far from windows, doors and vents, never in an enclosed or partly enclosed space (Honda EU2200i). CO alarms on every level of the home and outside sleeping areas (Honda EU2200i); Health Canada's minimum is at least one with battery backup, most important in the hallway outside the bedrooms (Health Canada CO). Store a generator with fuel in it away from furnaces, water heaters and dryers (Honda EU2200i).

## When no help is coming

- If the furnace won't stay lit on generator power, check polarity and the neutral-to-ground reading before anything else. Never bypass the flame sensor, pressure switch or limit switches to make it run (Goodman RS6621301 warns never to bypass the controls): they are what keep CO and fire out of the house.
- A furnace that has been opened for parts must never be fired again (see [Furnace teardown](#guides/teardown_furnace)).
- If fuel for the generator is short, heat one room instead: see [Staying warm](#guides/skill_staying_warm).
